caveats_register: OFF-BY-ONE STAMPS: the blind-S0 window contains 52 Mondays, but Monday 2026-04-20T00:00Z lies inside the frozen F1 1-day purge zone [2026-04-20,2026-04-21), so the schedule yields 51 discretionary decisions (F0=17, F1=17, F2=17). All frozen floors pass; the proposals' self-declared '>= 52 decisions in the screen window' (a5) and nominal '52' counts (a6, a8) should be corrected to 51 in W1 documentation. This is a documentation correction, not a redesign.

A8 FILL-REFERENCE SEMANTICS: OITD/TCH fill at the open of the 00:15Z bar at order release T+15m; the bar record becomes available at 00:30Z. Economically realizable and free of decision-time look-ahead, but it requires an explicit slot-open transaction-reference convention in the W1 engine; strict record-availability reads (the a5/a6 close-fill convention) avoid the issue.

STRESSED-COST MARGIN AT THE ADVERSARIAL CEILING: stressed drag <= 12% holds at all plausible churn (<= 6.05% at 1.0 one-way/stamp); the mathematical ceiling (full-book replacement every week, c=2.0) gives 12.09% at average tick rates - a corner that would itself fail the frozen realized-schedule gate at score time. For the hysteresis books (a8) the margin is wide; for the full-rebalance books (a5/a6) the score-time gate is the binding protection.

QUINTILE TURNOVER-SHARE MARGIN (a6): equal-weight 5-name books have an expected per-symbol turnover share of 20% vs the 25% floor - by symmetry only; churn concentration in one slot could breach, detected (never relaxed) by the frozen gate, as CAPVEL itself states.

MARK-PRICE GRANULARITY: no dedicated mark-price root exists; mark observations are the markPrice field of funding settlement rows (<= 8h staleness). EXITCAP's and OITD's declared 24h pairing tolerances are satisfiable at every stamp; consumers must document that mark stamps coincide with settlement stamps.

OI HISTORY STARTS 2025-07-01: all OI warmups are satisfiable (EXITCAP latest-snapshot; CAPVEL >= 26/>= 52 counts with +2/+3 margin at stamp 1; OITD 7-in-10d), but any post-hoc extension of OI lookbacks beyond ~54d before 2025-08-25 would be infeasible without new data (which would require an owner data-authority decision).

EXITCAP/LIQEPIS DROP-ONE WORDING: the drop symbol tie-break (ascending symbol id) is declared for the book but not restated in the drop-one rule, and 'renormalize the remaining side to 5 symbols per side (1/10)' is ambiguous (one symbol dropped total vs one per side). Pin both sentences before W1. CAPVEL/LIQPRO drop-one also needs an explicit tie-break (all held weights tie at 0.20). OITD/TCH drop-one is fully declared.

EXITCAP CONTROL ATTRIBUTION LABEL: the STATIC-SCALE placebo ranks OI_now / frozen_capacity_i (frozen per-symbol denominator), not literal raw OI scale; the detection logic is sound but the 'raw positioning scale' attribution sentence should be read as 'frozen-capacity normalization'.

SCORE-TIME-ONLY CHECKS: 'per-side membership >= 4 at >= 95% of stamps' (a8), 'signal availability >= 95%' (a8), and the Stage-A concentration gates depend on the realized signal/book and are NOT verifiable schedule-only; they are deferred to the W1 cost_feasibility gate and Stage-A, per design.

verdict_summary.note: All six pass every schedule-only feasibility item on the real snapshot. Caveats above are documentation/engineering pins, none of which weakens a frozen floor or requires proposal redesign.
